correctness.rationale: For any two independent unit plane rows, the singleton residual maps are rank-one orthogonal projectors with cross-trace r^2; batch gives zero and skip gives the identity. The one-step Rayleigh quotient of p0I+p1P1+p2P2 gives R exactly. The self-adjoint second-moment map has invariant span of the two rank-one projectors, represented by a nonnegative 2-by-2 matrix whose top eigenvalue yields Q, including one-mask boundary cases; positivity and its overlap with identity justify the asymptotic sup-and-root limit. Fixed-batch-weight minimization strictly balances singleton probabilities for 0<r<1. The resulting two affine slopes change sign at 1-2/w and sqrt(1-2/w). The exact rational witness w=4,c=1,r=3/5 has R_single=4/5, R_batch=3/4, Q_single=17/25, Q_batch=3/4; a two-step exact recurrence gives 68/125<9/16. Standalone verifier tests rational projectors, finite covariance recurrences and 169 distribution-grid cases. There are no empirical-to-infinite extrapolations in the proof.

value.rationale: Joint batch sampling distributions are a motivated unresolved algorithm-design parameter in Xie–Yang (2025), and batch size has measurable cost. The theorem supplies a natural complete classification of policies on the smallest nontrivial coherent system under an equal expected-work constraint, for both exact one-step worst expected squared error and exact long-run mean-square decay. Their optimal policies separate on a strictly positive, sharp coherence interval for every coupled-block premium w>2. At w=4,c=1,r=3/5 the short-horizon-optimal policy loses at every horizon k>=2, providing a tangible mathematical warning against training a sampler solely against its exact one-step loss. The result is a scoped benchmark, not a general high-dimensional theorem or implementation guarantee.
